purpose: Present confirmed Snapdragon CPU/NPU speed and energy trade-offs, then preview one prompt under automatic and fast settings. Speed tuning, Qualcomm AI Engine Direct and model routing are separate experiments.

visual_system.typography: locally bundled Manrope for the wordmark; local system sans serif for UI; monospace for metrics
visual_system.motion: screen entrance and answer preview; respects reduced motion
visual_system.navigation: one persistent three-step navigation; no secondary sidebar

screens.headline: Tune your model. For this machine.
screens.purpose: Identify the recorded target and model before exploring calibration.
screens.lead: Compare the measurements. Choose how it runs.
screens.provenance: Machine and recorded date are available in Benchmark evidence.

screens.headline: Automatic chose NPU. Speed chose CPU.
screens.purpose: Present the confirmed automatic-NPU versus CPU-fast comparison and its energy trade-off.
content: confirmed evidence dialog with historical screening
screens.comparison: Same Qwen3-0.6B Q4_0 weights, 512 input / 128 output tokens, battery-powered five alternating pairs. Native decode and full-trial energy have different intervals.
screens.empty_state: If confirmed provenance is unavailable, show a recoverable error instead of screening numbers.
screens.quality_status: Engine performance confirmed for this fixed workload; task quality not calibrated.

screens.headline: See the comparison flow.
screens.purpose: Finish with readable answers side by side; no file operations.
content: one shared prompt with example selector
one Run preview / Stop / Replay button
one split surface for Automatic setup and Local Turbo answers
screens.completion: Leave both answers visible on this final screen.
screens.layout: Prompt spans both answer columns. Equal-width answer columns share one surface and a single divider; stack on mobile. Model identity stays beside its answer; omit the redundant route explanation.
screens.progressive_disclosure: Keep the preview badge visible. Hide method, simulation details and calibration caveats under How this comparison works. Do not display empty metric rows.

timing.preview: Independent browser animation clock per answer; excludes queue time, freezes on completion, resets on stop/replay. Never an inference measurement or speedup.
timing.live: Use backend total_time_s with explicit source and scope; never substitute browser animation time.

screens.example_picker: Styled disclosure with selected-state buttons, outside-click dismissal, Escape, and keyboard focus restoration.
screens.empty_state: Empty answer areas retain their model headers and animation clocks; no placeholder prose.
screens.preview_explanation: Scripted preview using confirmed configuration labels. Clocks measure browser animation, not inference.

rules: Never present animated recorded results as a live benchmark.
Never use invented performance numbers or treat null as zero.
Never label screening gains as confirmed speedups; the main comparison comes from five alternating confirmation pairs.
Never infer verified NPU computation from a requested or reported device alone.
No duplicate navigation, unrelated marketing sections, or camera/Arduino workflow.
Preserve the same three-screen UX when a live provider is added, with explicit mode and evidence states.
One persistent mode badge. Benchmark evidence is available from the footer; task evidence belongs with the task result.
Do not animate the whole screen again on every state update.
The final comparison is about model responses; do not introduce files or file-management tasks.
Use equal animation pacing for preview lanes. Do not stage a fake speed or quality advantage.
Model routing requires separately measured model profiles and quality requirements; example roles are not real routing decisions.
Preserve page one's device visual. Keep qairt results pending until actual device measurements and task checks arrive.
